hook: SCP-2998 opens with an apology from the records office: the file is infected, and you will have to click through a series of false versions before reaching the real one. Take that at face value and keep going, because each iteration is a different kind of story wearing the same item number. It is long and gets grim in places, so set aside a proper sitting.
whyItMatters: Its tag list runs from science fiction and cosmic horror to crime and military fiction, and that range is earned, since each false iteration really does switch genre. It pushes the revision-chain format well past simple escalation, through an invasion, a collapsed civilization and a page that can no longer be read. The RAISA notice that frames the whole thing turns the familiar act of clicking to the next version into part of the plot.
thingsToNotice:
The early iterations are first contact by eavesdropping: two D-class with a rare nerve bundle feel what the signal carries and explain it in gangland terms: a vast being called Adidal is punishing Ruhar, who attacked Adidal's family, by keeping it alive in agony and broadcasting that agony to the whole universe forever. Then the screaming stops, the eight D-class watching it seize, overpower their escort in unexplained unison and flee, and a later footnote reveals Ruhar had died and the D-class carrying something of it were hunted down and killed within three days anyway. The Keter version follows with an alien craft at L5, signals that turn listeners into drones, captives who bleed from the nose, ears and eyes and kill themselves with their teeth, and a site overrun hours after an interview.

Next comes a document written by a theocratic successor to the Foundation, ordering crusaders to kill, to make martyrs of their own captured, and to send enemies to Recycling Duty amid food shortages, with Maria Jones and David Rosen listed among the heretics. In the garbled copy of that file, the footnotes hide the two of them finding each other on the dead network: Rosen is holed up under Site-62C, where the occupiers, he notes, have even taken 682 and other Keters off Earth, and Jones sends him to retrieve 055 and fit the peg into the hole as a last-ditch contingency. After the fully redacted page and the narrator's line about the past, the final file is dull: a harmless white noise whose exposure causes hallucinations treatable with thiamine, signed by Jones as RAISA Director, which implies their gamble rewrote history. Its closing promise of a breakthrough in decoding within three months suggests the whole thing could start again.

related.note: In the footnote exchange, Rosen is sent to find it at Site-62C as part of a last-resort plan.
